item.title: The Sports Report - December 2021 - Thank you all for a great year!
item.description:
Having trouble viewing this email? View it as a Web page.

New Year - New Website

After starting in mid-December, the content from CRPDSports.org is moving to a new home on columbusrecparks.com. By unifying our web presence, we allow our users to become more connected with the department as a whole! Combining our sports community and the larger Columbus Recreation and Parks community allows us to simplify communications, saving time and resources. 

Our sports facilities and rentals pages, including Lou Berliner Sports Park, have already moved over to the new site. The adult softball leagues and tournament pages have also gone live. The rest of our adult sports and youth sports pages will be migrated over in the coming weeks. Our Marketing/Engagement Team is hopeful to have all of the pages moved over by Jan. 21.

From Our Adult Sports Team

A very busy 2021 programming year came to an end earlier this month with the completion of fall basketball and volleyball. The Adult Sports Team wants to send a big ‘thank you’ to all of the different areas within the Sports Office who helped make this year a big success! 

Even while most areas of the Sports Office were short handed, the Field Staff, Grounds Crew, Marketing/Engagement Team and Front Office Staff all came together and played an important role in what we accomplished throughout the year.

For the entire year, we had 1,215 teams participate in softball leagues, 636 in basketball leagues, 163 in volleyball leagues and 50 in kickball leagues. In total, that is over 2,000 teams that participated in CRPD leagues! Well over half of our league seasons saw an increase in teams from comparable 2019 and 2020 leagues.

Well done team!!

From Charnon Barnes

As we approach the end of the year I want to highlight some folks and amazing things we’ve done this year. I want to give a huge shout out to Zach Davis and Jessica Pallante for all of their help in organizing and overseeing the McCoy Soccer League. We had over 600 participants from 14 sites in the league this year! We are still working through the pandemic and our center staff and volunteers made this season a success.  We had over 1,675 participants overall in youth soccer programming. I appreciate everything you all do to provide this amazing program to your communities!

I am so proud of our willingness and ability to support our community. This year, we gave out over 680 PLAY Scholarships for Youth Sports equaling over $24,500 in scholarships over three sports seasons - 21/22 soccer, spring baseball/softball, fall baseball/softball. This is absolutely incredible! Our efforts to increase access to quality and affordable youth sports programs never ceases to amaze me. I am so excited to see what we are capable of in 2022.

Another huge win for Youth Sports was being awarded the NRPA Youth Sports and Play Grant for $40,000. This grant is going to be used to replace fencing on Diamond #3 at Sammons Park. Also with this grant, we were given a year of free coaches training opportunities through the Positive Coaching Alliance. Positive Coaching Alliance (PCA) provides research-based training and resources for coaches to ensure a positive youth development experience for all kids, in all communities by using sports to teach life lessons. We will be rolling out these training sessions in the near future. 

Once again, thank you, thank you, THANK YOU for all your hard work and dedication. These successes could not have been achieved without you! I am very excited to see what the future of Youth Sports has in store. 

Cheers to you and to 2022!

item.title: The Internal Sports Report - November 2021
item.description:
Having trouble viewing this email? View it as a Web page.

It is with immense mixed emotions we announce Chloe Meisner will be leaving us on Nov. 30. After two and a half years with us, she has taken a full time position at Franklin Park Conservatory. Chloe started with the Sports Office as our marketing and engagement intern. After hitting it out of the park with Sports, she moved into an internship and later a part-time position with Community Relations. Her major contributions include the summer camp website and the new ColumbusRecParks.com site. 

The dedication, energy, talent and spirit she brought to Columbus Recreation and Parks is going to be extremely hard to replace. We are sad that she is leaving us, but we are also extremely happy for her. We can’t wait to see what this next chapter holds for you.

If you get a chance, send her an email or slack message and wish her the best of luck in her new adventure.

Thank you to everyone on our team for the part you played in making our 2021 adult softball leagues a big success! Our final fall leagues came to a close earlier this month and we had outstanding participation throughout the year.

We now look forward to a very busy ‘indoor season!’ Adult basketball and volleyball team registration takes place in December and leagues begin the first week of January. It was around this time last year that our facilities were shut down, so our team is very excited to have our gyms open this winter. In addition to our leagues and regular permits, we have several other sports and events using our court space, including dodgeball, futsal, field hockey, prayer groups, cheerleading and the recently completed video game show!

Basketball registration is closing on Nov. 30 and registration for all centers is currently around 1078 participants. Please get out to your communities and let them know about our basketball leagues. We are offering the Play Scholarship for Youth Sports for these leagues at every center. With the scholarship, the price is $25 per child. If there is a family in need of extra assistance, please register them to the waiting list and let the Youth Sports Team know and we will take care of the rest. Please let us know if you have any questions regarding basketball registration. We are very excited to get back onto the court!

2021 has proven to be one of the busiest years ever for the Sports Office. Participation at Lou Berliner Sports Park was at an all-time high and we experienced larger tournaments than ever before. On top of this, our athletic complexes, prime facilities and youth routes continued to be used on a daily basis. Our Grounds Crew team did an exceptional job in maintaining all of these fields/courts, preparing them on a daily basis and doing whatever was needed for the department. With that being said, all of this was done and maintained with only a fraction of our regular year round staff. A big THANK YOU is deserved to everyone that was part of the grounds team in 2021—none of this would have been possible without you!

Lastly, a special shoutout to Spencer Garrison. Spencer has accepted a full time position as a Sports Field Maintenance Supervisor within the Sports Office. Spencer has shown tremendous growth and willingness to learn throughout his three plus years with the Sports Office. We look forward to him taking on a larger role and becoming a leader within our grounds crew and the department.

We want to recognize one of our staff members for their immense contributions to our success during this difficult year. Handling a variety of roles, Chris Denney has stepped up throughout the year, doing “whatever it takes” to keep our operation running smoothly. Chris recently returned to his Field Supervisor position while still juggling some additional duties. Great job Chris—a good example of a selfless team player!

Luanne Kornegay Retiring After 34 Years

Lu started with the Sports Office in 1988 and this is what she wanted share with those in the middle or just starting their career:

Sun up to sun down, dirt to turf, paper to web, "All games are cancelled" to an automated rain line, I've worked through it all. I am extremely grateful to my mentors, past and present, who advised, coached and shared the same vision and passion for the Sports Office throughout my journey. To the rest of the staff, thank you for putting up with the red pen, my "back when" stories, and "I'm retiring"....every year since 2016. Keep up the outstanding work you do for the Columbus Sports community, we are the best around. Remember this, coming from a veteran, "You've gotta love what you do to get there." AND I AM THERE...rounding third and heading for home.

Staffing Updates

There have been many changes to our staff recently, and we wanted to recognize a few. 

Jay Clark has led our field staff for the last several months after working in a variety of roles in the Sports Office. Jay recently accepted a new position at Ohio State and will be starting next week. 

Ben Fort is our longest tenured field rep, and he recently started a full time position at Cardinal Health. Ben is going to remain on our staff and fill in on some weekend shifts for the foreseeable future. 

Sydney Hammond has been working with us since the summer and has become a crucial asset to the Front Desk team! Sydney received an Internship with Disney and will be heading to Orlando, Florida in February! She will continue working with us until then, but make sure to wish her the best of luck in Florida with this experience and to enjoy the warm weather!

Adult Sports

It’s hard to believe, but October is already winding down, and with that our 2021 softball leagues are coming to a close. The first fall softball playoff games will take place this Friday night!

We had an outstanding turnout for our 2021 softball leagues with 1,215 total teams participating throughout the year. In the past ten years there was only one single year in which we had more total teams than this year (2018). Thanks to our wonderful field staff for all of their hard work throughout the year. We had a lot of turnover with our field supervisor and field rep roles this year and had numerous individuals step into prominent roles with our leagues. Everyone did an exceptional job and handled everything in stride!

Fall Baseball

Congratulations to the Driving Park Bandits who won our Inaugural Pony League Championship! The Pony League would not have happened without the time and dedication of Johnny Wright, Dealow Morgan, Will Fant and the Schiller and Driving Park staff. Thank you to all the coaches and CRPD staff who dedicated their time to the youth in their communities.

Youth Sports Training

As you heard in Jack's weekly video, the Youth Sports team will be providing training to all staff regarding the expectations and standards for CRPD Youth Sports. We will discuss our mission statement, philosophy and code of conduct expected for volunteers, coaches and staff. We don’t just offer sports, we offer our youth opportunities to learn life skills that will stay with them throughout their lives. It is imperative that we create an environment that is positive for our youth participants and community. Be on the lookout for more information.

A New External Newsletter

Beginning in November, Columbus Recreation and Parks will be consolidating our email newsletters into a weekly updates blast. Each week, we will cover programs in Nature, Wellness, Creativity and Community. Make sure you get these emails by signing up here.

Each year, Americans observe National Hispanic Heritage Month from Sept. 15 to Oct. 15 by celebrating the histories, cultures and contributions of American citizens whose ancestors came from Spain, Mexico, the Caribbean and Central and South America.

The observation started in 1968 as Hispanic Heritage Week under President Lyndon Johnson and was expanded by President Ronald Reagan in 1988 to cover a 30-day period. It was enacted into law on Aug. 17, 1988, on the approval of Public Law 100-402.

The day of Sept.15 is significant because it is the anniversary of independence for Latin American countries such as Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras and Nicaragua. In addition, Mexico and Chile celebrate their independence days on September 16 and September 18, respectively. https://www.hispanicheritagemonth.gov/about/

When celebrating the Hispanic culture, you have to talk about soccer and the vital role it plays in daily life, the sense of pride, passion, and belonging that it inspires. Similarly, you cannot talk about soccer without honoring the role of Hispanic players in writing its history. How would soccer history be without Diego Maradona, Hugo Sánchez, Lionel Messi, or Pele? 

https://www.soccer.com/guide/celebrate-hispanic-heritage-month-through-soccer

2021 Softball Tournaments

As our 2021 tournament schedule winds down, we wanted to highlight and recognize the many accomplishments to date. So far this year, we have had 251 total teams participate in eight adult softball tournaments. Several tournaments have seen an increase in teams compared to 2019 and 2020 tournaments.

With many staff changes this year, we have been able to train several new staff members on tournament operations and introduce them to new responsibilities. Over the past year, Jake Diefenthaler became a tournament director for the first time and has done a great job handling his first few tournaments. Recently, Hadley Bloemeke got her feet wet with responsibilities at the Screwball and Nite Owl Classic tournaments, and handled many duties including providing exceptional customer service!

Also, a big thank you to the countless part time staff members and the entire Grounds Crew team that have helped us run many outstanding events during these unprecedented times.

We wrap up our 2021 tournament season with the upcoming tournaments: Nite Owl Classic II on Sept. 24, Friday Night Frights on Oct. 29 and Turkey Bowl on Nov. 13–14.

It’s time for Soccer For Success Training! This year, we will be doing the training in person and it will be broken into 2 days: Tuesday, Sept. 21 and Thursday, Sept. 23. Both trainings will be at Blackburn Community Center 12–2:30 p.m. 

This will be a classroom and active training. Please dress accordingly. You must attend both days to be fully certified and receive funding and equipment from the grant.

Zach Davis, DaShaunta Drew, Ryan Hicks and Alex Passas. 

These folks are the first people to complete their Soccer For Success training!! They were focused and engaged during the training and I couldn’t have asked for a better way to start the season!!

Grounds Crew's Hard Work for NAGAAA

During the NAGAAA Gay Softball World Series, our Grounds Crew had several members that embodied the core values of Columbus Recreation and Parks. We hosted a five-day event at Lou Berliner Sports Park consisting of thousands of participants and spectators. Everyone did a great job coming together doing whatever it takes to put on a great event for our customers.

One of the employees that has embraced those values is Shae van Gassen, who has brought a selfless attitude and go-getter mentality all season. Those traits continued into the NAGAAA event, voluntarily working over to jump in to help her coworkers no matter the task at hand. Another employee that really stepped up was Charles “Buckets” Butler. He took lead on detailed work in the stands leading up to the tournament and did an excellent job. Buckets really took pride in what he was doing and asked questions to make sure he was doing a quality job..

Not only did Colin Roberts work his normal shift Monday at the soccer parks, he also didn't hesitate to stay over that evening to help out with event setup going into the tournament’s first day. Taylor Barrett moved her schedule around on short notice and also stayed over several days to ensure we stayed caught up on all of our core services throughout the event. Taylor and Dan Perks worked together to have the park in great shape going into play the next morning each evening they worked. Dan takes pride in the work he does and always strives to put out quality work on fields for our customers.

Lastly, Spencer Garrison was everywhere throughout the entire event. He balanced staff management, core services and also did whatever he could to assist the tournament staff. He displayed fantastic customer service and was a great representation of Columbus Recreation and Parks. Despite being short on staffing, each member of the Grounds Crew pulled together to help one another. Thank you to everyone involved!

Staff Updates

Kyla Burnett recently replaced a long time staff member, Casey Meddles, at the front desk. In the first few weeks of being on our team she has done an amazing job. She has already mastered most of the responsibilities at the front office and is always looking to help fellow staff members. We are grateful to have her on our staff and look forward to seeing her contributions moving forward.

Lauren Tischer joined our Field Staff in the spring, and has taken on many different roles over the summer season. Over the last two months, she has become one of our primary Field Reps for our leagues at Lou Berliner Sports Park, Anheuser-Busch Sports Park and our athletic complexes. Because of her efforts, we have given her the opportunity to assist our supervisors as a Rover out in the field. She will be trained in this role over the month of September by our veteran supervisor, Chris Harley. We are excited to see the continued progressions Lauren will make this fall season!

item.description:

As most of you should know, the Sports Office has been merged into the Community Recreation Division. This integration of Sports into the Community Recreation Division will help build stronger relationships between each of the Community Recreation Division sections. A piece of this stronger relationship comes in the form of the new ACE Awards. The Community Recreation Division has an opportunity for ComRec Staff to recognize those who went above and beyond in customer service. Anyone can nominate a group, team or individual. This is available to all Community Recreation staff, part-time and full-time! To nominate someone for an ACE Award, please be sure to give a specific example of their excellent customer service.

Also, a Community Recreation Division Employee of the Month will be chosen out of each month’s ACE Award nominees. In last week’s video, Jack announced the July Employee of the Month: Shaun Ballard from Scioto Southland Community Center. 

Take an opportunity to congratulate Shaun and don’t forget to submit your ACE Award nominees for August!

NOMINATE

Summer II sports leagues are officially underway and we had an unbelievable turnout for the session! All time records were hit with 138 basketball teams and 264 softball teams participating in the current Summer II session!

All areas of the Sports Office play a huge role in our successes, but we wanted to give a big shout out to our outstanding Field Staff team. We have had a large amount of turnover within the last year, but our team has not missed a beat. Many obstacles have been overcome and it is great to have so many team members willing to help out when needed. Recently we had a basketball scorekeeper call into the office to highlight one of our field reps and let us know what an outstanding job she has been doing recently. He said she was always accessible and visible to our teams and rental groups, always willing to help out and go above and beyond what is needed. Great job Emily Czyzewski, as well as our entire field staff!

It’s back to school season and we are preparing our fall season sports. As you all know, we are offering fall baseball and softball. We are excited because for the first time we will have some Pony teams. Dealow Morgan, Johnny Wright and Will Fant were the driving force behind creating the Pony division. The Pony division is for youth ages 14–18. We are very excited to be able to offer another teenage sports program and are looking forward to seeing them play. 

Fall soccer begins soon and we are thrilled to offer another season of Soccer For Success. Soccer For Success is an “after-school program that is proven to help kids establish healthy habits and develop critical life skills through trained coach-mentors and community engagement.” In order for your center to receive funding, training is mandatory. Centers that are involved in the McCoy League will need to send a representative to participate. We will offer training on Aug. 31 and Sept. 2 at Blackburn Community Center. The training will consist of classroom and active training. Even if you are not participating in the McCoy League this fall but plan on offering soccer programming, you can still participate in the program. Please let Char Barnes know if you are interested. 

The HBCU Classic for Columbus weekend is coming up and there are several events available throughout the weekend. Columbus Recreation and Parks will be hosting a Youth Football Skills and Drills Clinic on Aug. 28 at Lincoln Tower Park at 12 p.m. Mike Doss, Beanie Wells, Obie Stillwell and a few other former players and coaches will be in attendance. We still have spots open for kids ages 10–15 in ActiveNet (#79818). Please get your kids registered as soon as possible. There will be swag bags and a free ticket to the game for every child that registers. We are also still looking for a few volunteers. All volunteers will receive a free ticket to the game. Please let Char Barnes know if you are interested.

EMAIL CHAR

Throughout our busy season the Grounds Crew have had several members take on additional responsibilities. Shae van Gassen learned how to operate all of our tractors and skid loader, as well as the fertilizer spreader. She has also done a great job as a leader for our new hires, handling training and setting a good example through great work ethic. Another employee, Jalon Toy has done a great job stepping in for Eric, continuing our Busch Park and youth route field maintenance. Jalon has also taken Dan Perks under his wing and trained him on our dirt grooming practices. Not only has Dan been learning about our dirt field maintenance, but he has also demonstrated great qualities as an employee, keeping a positive attitude regardless of the task at hand. Lastly, Charles “Buckets” Butler has shown the ability to be flexible with his schedule and is always looking to help the team out. Charles has been with us since the spring and has been a key member throughout the 2021 season.

Park and Recreation Month

Since 1985, America has celebrated July as the nation’s official Park and Recreation Month. Created by the National Recreation and Park Association (NRPA), Park and Recreation Month specifically highlights the vital and powerful role local park and recreation professionals, such as our staff at Columbus Recreation and Parks Department, play in building stronger, more vibrant and more resilient communities all across the country. 

Parks are at the center of so many experiences and memories — moments that park and recreation professionals help make happen. Our local parks are often our first experiences in nature, our introduction to a favorite hobby or physical activity. They are places to gather with friends and family, spaces to celebrate life’s special moments, spots of respite and healing, sites that connect us with essential community services, and so much more.

Adult Sports

It was a beautiful July Fourth weekend for Columbus Sports at Lou Berliner Sports Park as Team CRPD took the championship after scoring big at The Columbus Classic presented by White Castle. With a stacked line-up, the marketing group led off with a line drive to the Columbus Sports community getting the word out and promoting through social media. On deck, our all-star Grounds Crew set the stage by prepping fields and getting the park in tip-top shape. In the hole, our Parking Crew/Tournament Operations welcomed thousands of participants, family and friends at the entrance to the park. Batting clean-up, the Programming Team knocked it out of the park bringing it all together. No wasted peanuts and crackerjacks this weekend folks, these sports enthusiasts will be back for the ol’ ball game.

Youth Sports

July is Park and Recreation Month. I think it’s fitting that our month is in the middle of the summer because I think summer is where we shine. I am so proud to be a part of a department that makes it their goal to make sure that all children have an exciting, safe and fun time during their summer break. This was my first year being an administrator for sports camps, and let me say this, it was tough. Lots of new challenges and firsts for me, but with the help of some very helpful and dedicated people, we were able to offer some amazing camps. So this is a shout out to you all, my CRPD family, for continuing to do the amazing work you do for our communities. 

Here’s a letter we received from a parent of Next Level Basketball Camp.

Good Morning Anna and Char, 

I'm Kenny R. Hampton and I'm the parent of Kenneth Hampton, 3rd grade participant at the Next Level hoops camp. He attended the session a couple of weeks ago and is participating this week as well. 

I wanted to inform you both of the great experience we've had as a family due to the great leadership team in place at the facility. Oftentimes, many will submit complaints but fail to share compliments so we wanted to compliment you and your team for doing a great job and providing a clean and safe environment for our child. 

Keep up the great work!

Thanks, 

Kenny R. Hampton

Welcome Devin and Matt!

Devin Zinser is our most recent new hire for our field staff. Devin is currently a student at Ohio State University and will be interning with us this fall season. In addition to assisting us he will be working for the varsity football team at Jerome High School.

Matt Wray joined our Field Staff in February and has been very involved and contributed greatly to the efforts of our operation. Matt graduated from Ohio State University this spring, majoring in sports industry. Matt was recently moved into a Rover position on our team and we are grateful to have him in this new role moving forward! 

Farewell to Bill and Eric!

Bill Erwin accepted a maintenance position with Waverly schools. Bill has been a key member of the Grounds Crew on special project work, as well as maintaining the athletic complexes. His problem solving and upbeat personality will be greatly missed.

After a decade with us, Eric Drummond will be taking his talents to the City of Westerville as a member of their Park Maintenance staff. Eric is as skilled as they come, maintaining dirt infields, handling the maintenance at Anheuser-Busch Sports Park and at our youth fields throughout the city. 

These two individuals were important parts that helped keep the Grounds Crew running smoothly and will be missed. Thank you both for everything you’ve done!

Happy Pride Month!

June is Pride Month and the programs and facilities of Columbus Recreation and Parks Sports Office provide a safe and inclusive place for all people to play. Our facilities have hosted many games, leagues and tournaments that connect the LGBTQIA+ community through sports.

 

Lou Berliner Sports Park hosted the Gay Softball World Series in 2010 and 2015. In 2020, GSWS was going to return to Berliner, but due to the pandemic, the event was rescheduled for August of this year. Beginning in 2017, Stonewall Sports Columbus began renting our facilities for their leagues, including kickball and dodgeball. Since 1986, the Columbus Lesbian and Gay Softball Association league has been playing in our parks. They started at Berliner and now play at Anheuser-Busch Sports Park. In 2019, we hosted International Gay Rugby's Capital City Rugby Cup at Kilbourne Run Sports Park.

 

Columbus is a welcoming city and the Sports Office is no different. Our programs, parks and facilities are open for all.

Thank You Field Staff!

Summer basketball and volleyball are underway and we had a great turnout for the session. We have 199 total basketball and volleyball teams participating this summer which is just short of our all-time record for summer session. This follows our successful spring indoor season which also had a great turnout after we re-opened our leagues in March. 

 

Much of the success of these recent leagues can be attributed to the hard work of our outstanding Field Staff. Since our facilities and leagues have opened up, we have had several new team members come aboard. Many were interested in quickly taking on more responsibility, including getting trained on Field Rep duties. We wanted to recognize each and every one of our Field Supervisors and Field Reps who have taken care of our leagues these last two sessions!

Youth Sports

With folks getting vaccines and restrictions being lifted, things are starting to get back to “normal” and we were able to offer Baseball, Softball and Tee Ball to our youth this season. Compliment from a Customer

“This past weekend my team competed in the Heart of Ohio Sr. Softball tournament. I wanted to take a minute to share my appreciation for Kevin's quality efforts before and during the tournament. His communications in advance of the tournament were clear, concise and allowed managers like myself to have a thorough understanding of what to expect and when and where we needed to be.

During the tournament I noticed he was sought out frequently for questions and guidance and he remained calm and always made himself available. He was extremely patient and accommodating even under pressure. My team plays in a lot of tournaments each year and this one was run as smoothly as any I've ever seen. A combination of bad weather and a team dropping out at the last minute caused Kevin to have to adjust on the fly and he even handled those events seamlessly. 

It was unfortunate the tournament had to be stopped short due to atrocious Sunday weather, but it was the right decision and Kevin's communication around the stoppage was equally clear and concise.  

You have a beautiful complex, but even a great complex won't bring teams back if the format is poor and the tournament is poorly run. We won't hesitate to return next year and we'll gladly spread the word to other teams, and Kevin's organizational and communication skills are a big part of the reason.” - Rick

Mental Health and Youth Sports

May is Mental Health Awareness Month. When we think of youth sports, we must think of more than the physical aspect of sports. We must think of the WHOLE youth athlete—physical and mental. There are many benefits to youth sports for our young athletes. Physical activity has been proven to increase endorphins, reduce the stress hormone cortisol and stimulate norepinephrine, which improves mood. Here ways that youth sports can benefit young athletes:

  • Socialization - It is easy for kids to bond over similar interests and work together on a singular goal. This is the perfect recipe for creating friendships. Feeling a sense of acceptance and belonging is important for children. When kids feel supported by their teammates and their coaches it helps to build a sense of community. 
  • Confidence - Making the team, making a free throw or throwing a strike can increase a child’s confidence. Those small wins can help to teach other important lessons about hard work, practice and patience. This lesson will carry them throughout their lives. 
  • Resilience - Sometimes a child will learn more from a loss than a win. This teaches kids that they can make mistakes and that they don’t have to be perfect. Teaching children how to continue practicing and working hard even after a loss is a very important lesson for children to have for adulthood. 
  • Body Image - Children are constantly bombarded with images of the beauty and body standards that are often unrealistic and manipulated. Sports gives children an opportunity to see strong, powerful bodies in different shapes and sizes. Female athletes, in particular, have been shown to benefit from positive feelings about their bodies, regardless of whether they conform to society’s standards of female beauty, according to Psychology Today. 

As you can see, having positive sports experiences benefits a child's physical and mental health. CRPD currently has registration open for our soccer program that begins in the fall. We hope to see you on the field.

Grounds Crew Updates

The Grounds Crew has brought on four new employees recently: Jackson VanDyke, Brendan Eagan, Adam Ruggles and Capell Miller. They are all studying in the sports management field and will be working with us through the summer. They are looking forward to having a unique experience on the Grounds Crew at Lou Berliner Sports Park. If you see them around at the park, please give them a warm welcome!

The Grounds Crew would also like to recognize Leslie Brown as she embarks on her journey to Alaska for a summer internship. Both her bright personality and determined work ethic made Leslie somebody we all enjoyed having around. She had a positive impact, not only on the Grounds Crew, but also the customers at our parks. Leslie was a key member of our team and will be missed by all!

April Program Spotlight

E3 Sports Academy at Driving Park

Driving Park’s E3 Sports Program was created from the minds of Dealow Morgan, assistant manager, at Driving Park Community Center and his associate ISA contract professor, Dr. Malcolm Cash. This initiative began around eight years ago as a Saturday school project to help tutor and mentor inner-city youth. Using sports, something the students already had an interest in and knowledge of, the program focused on improving upon writing and public speaking skills. Morgan, utilizing a background in broadcasting, and Cash would show the students all the work that goes into presenting the subject matter.

What began as a weekend project has now blossomed into opportunities for these students. With four to five students in September 2020, the participants were given a chance to meet the play-by-play and color commentators while attending a Columbus Blue Jackets game. Continue Reading...

Adult Sports

It’s great to have all of our adult sports programs back in full swing this spring! A very successful spring softball season completes on Thursday, April 22 and summer session begins on Friday, April 23. Spring basketball and volleyball leagues continue through the middle of May, concluding with the Champ of Champs Tournament presented by Jimmy John’s the week of May 17.

A special shout out to Jake Diefenthaler and Chris Denney for their help in organizing last week's field rep meeting, and to Kevin Ohms and Steve Baxter for their help in training some of the new field staff members. Continue reading...

Youth Sports

Summer Camp is quickly approaching and we are getting excited! The summer of 2020 required our department to be creative in finding the best way to provide camp. I was very proud of our department, specifically Community Recreation, for finding a way to provide this invaluable service to our community. I always tell people that summer camp is where we really shine! 

Renny Tyson will be the new Next Level Basketball Camp Director this summer and I wanted to sit down and chat with him about his plans for summer camp and where his love for basketball and coaching began. Continue Reading...

Grounds Crew

Sammons Park is getting a full renovation. This major project started last year with Diamond 2 getting some much needed field work. Diamond 1 is the focus of our attention right now, bringing it back to life. The fence was repaired and is getting all new fence capping. The old cinder block dugouts were removed and new dugouts are being installed with new fencing and benches. We are working on re-establishing the field to a 90’ baseball field. The arc and field layout has been set up and we have removed all of the overgrown sod. We are developing a grade plan now in preparation to begin grade work, consisting of raising parts of the field about 10" and finishing the field with 3-4" of new infield material.

Women's History Month

In 1987, Congress passed Pub. L. 100-9 which designated the month of March 1987 as Women's History Month. Women's History Month highlights the contributions of women to events in history and contemporary society. Women throughout history have been making contributions that have changed and progressed all while not receiving credit for their work. Women have been working full-time jobs, taking care of families and fighting for their communities without credit or recognition for decades. It’s time we give these women their flowers and celebrate the women that have inspired and paved the way for others. We asked some of our staff what women inspire them. See what Suzanne Schwartz, DaShaunta Drew, Morgan Wilson and Charnon Barnes have to say. Continue Reading...

Adult Sports

In honor of Women’s History Month, our theme has been to highlight women in sports. Our leagues are home to many outstanding female athletes and to help grasp just how many women we have participating in our programs, here are some numbers to consider from 2019, our last full year of league play. 100% of our volleyball teams are women’s or co-ed teams, 44% of our softball teams are women’s or co-ed and 7% of our basketball teams are women’s. Incredibly, that is well over 1,000 teams in our adult sports leagues that had women participating. Way to represent, ladies!

After many months without leagues, our spring adult leagues are finally underway! All of our spring basketball, softball and volleyball leagues started up over the past week and the session is off to a great start. Continue reading...

Youth Sports

In 1972, Title IX was enacted. The civil rights law states that:

“No person in the United States shall, on the basis of sex, be excluded from participation in, be denied the benefits of, or be subjected to discrimination under any education program or activity receiving Federal financial assistance.”

Athletic programs are considered educational programs and activities. Title IX gives girls and women athletes the right to participate in athletic programming from any educational institution, elementary through college,  that receives federal funding. With this law, the world of sports opened up for girls and women. 

While there are many girls' and women’s sports and teams, we are still struggling with equity within sports. The lessons gained through sports are meaningful to both boys and girls. Sports help to develop healthy habits and important life skills. Yet many girls are left out of the game. Continue Reading...

Castle's Corner

As many of you know, Justin Waters and Jeff Derr left Columbus Recreation and Parks Department for other career opportunities. We will miss their hard work and dedication but are very happy for them as they explore new opportunities. Mindfulness

The past 12 months have shown us the best and the worst of society. We’ve seen people helping their neighbors and communities but we’ve also seen social injustice and extreme poverty. In Amanda Gorman’s poem, "The Hill We Climb," she states:

"If we merge mercy with might,
And might with right
Then love becomes our legacy"

We have to try and work hard to make the changes we want to see in the world. We need to give corrections with mercy and understanding to people during their growth and journey. We have to try hard to do what is right—for all people—even if the journey is uncomfortable and long. By doing what is right for all, we spread tolerance, acceptance and love. The generations to come will be the legacy of the hard work we do today.

Mindfulness

Breathe, Stretch, Shake, Let It Go!!

Some of you will recognize this phrase as the title and chorus from the colorful bad boy rapper turned pastor, Ma$e. He retired from rap during the height of his career because he did not feel like his music was representing who he truly was as a person and leader. After education and reevaluation, he returned to music with this song. Breathe, Stretch, Shake, Let It Go was on his comeback album called “Welcome Back.”

It serves as a reminder that when you are going through tough times, to just take a pause and breathe. Do not hurry to action. Instead, evaluate the situation and then act with positive intention. Do not hold onto grudges and anger. Holding onto past issues will prevent you from moving forward. So be like Ma$e and Breathe, Stretch, Shake, Let It Go!

"Adversity, in the right culture, leads to tremendous growth." - Ryan DeMay

The Sports Office is dedicated to connecting people to their passions through sports by providing high quality sports programming and facilities to the residents and visitors of Columbus.

We hope by telling your stories through sharing your successes, Gold Standards Achievements and updates on programs, this monthly publication will strengthen the internal sports community. 

If you have a program update, success story, or a Gold Standard Achievement, please let us know by emailing Jeff Tilley.

Mindfulness

Breathe, Stretch, Shake, Let It Go!!

Some of you will recognize this phrase as the title and chorus from the colorful bad boy rapper turned pastor, Ma$e. He retired from rap during the height of his career because he did not feel like his music was representing who he truly was as a person and leader. After education and reevaluation, he returned to music with this song. Breathe, Stretch, Shake, Let It Go was on his comeback album called “Welcome Back.”

It serves as a reminder that when you are going through tough times, to just take a pause and breathe. Do not hurry to action. Instead, evaluate the situation and then act with positive intention. Do not hold onto grudges and anger. Holding onto past issues will prevent you from moving forward. So be like Ma$e and Breathe, Stretch, Shake, Let It Go!
